glosses: A person or company that sells insurance.
A legal document outlining a particular insurance cover for an insured entity for a given risk.
Something that protects or safeguards.
Describing a life insurance policy that insures two individuals' lives, payable either on a first death or last survivor basis.
Describing a joint life insurance policy that pays out in the event that both of the lives assured have died (not necessarily at the same time).
A form of insurance on the life of a person, whereby if the person dies then the insurance policy pays out a sum of money to the beneficiary (such as a person's family).
Of a policyholder, covered by a particular insurance policy or insurer at a specific point in time.
Fully paid (for).
Full-fledged, wholehearted.
Of an insurance policy, still in force but with the policyholder no longer paying any premiums (typically resulting in a reduced sum assured).

To place insurance on the contract that insures something (allowing the insurer to offset risk in the same way the insuree did).
Describing a joint life insurance policy that pays out in the event that both of the lives assured have died (not necessarily at the same time).
The practice of choosing to bear a risk oneself rather than taking out insurance with a third party (an insurance company).
Describing a life insurance policy that insures a single individual's life.

An addition.
A serving of drink used to top up an existing glass.

Additional credit purchased for a mobile phone.

An insurance product for covering unforeseen losses incurred while travelling, either internationally or domestically.

The ratio of the RMS value to the absolute mean of a sinusoidal wave (especially to that of an alternating current).
Any of several functions that describe the unknown internal state of a particle.
The emissivity of a material.
A function that describes the scattering power of an atom as function of the scattering angle.
A factor describing the stress distribution of a body.
The geometry of an object, especially in engineering design; configuration.
Military and industrial facilities situated in the same place.
A nation's armed forces and industries (especially those supplying weapons and other materiel) collectively, regarded as a strong vested interest exerting great influence on the government.
Of a product, immediately, without intervention from the customer.
Outside the box; unconventionally: outside the limits of conventional thinking.
Used other than figuratively or idiomatically: See out of, the, box.
Someone not directly involved in a transaction; an entity beyond the seller (first party) and customer (second party).
Someone only incidentally or tangentially connected to an incident or dispute; someone other than the principals; a bystander or independent witness.
A political party in opposition to the main parties in a two-party system.
A person or party not directly involved with an arrangement, in contrast to active parties, characteristically the first party (producer) and second party (consumer).
The part of a contractually due sum that is paid or received in advance for a good, service or social security.
